movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Choice Scarf Victini functions as a niche late-game cleaner and revenge killer, due to its ability to outspeed Pokemon such as Tapu Koko and Mega Lopunny as well as threaten important defensive pieces such as Ferrothorn and Gholdengo with V-create. U-turn is used to gain momentum on switch-ins such as Heatran, Alomomola, and Raging Bolt that would otherwise reliably answer it. Trick is used in order to cripple defensive switch-ins such as Alomomola, Toxapex, and Ting-Lu, allowing teammates to break through them more reliably. Bolt Strike is an option to hit Water-types such as Toxapex and Alomomola as well as Moltres and Mega Charizard Y, while Final Gambit allows Victini to trade for would-be answers such as Landorus-T and Garchomp. 252 HP EVs are only used on Final Gambit sets in order to maximise its damage against foes such as the aforementioned Landorus-T and Gliscor.

Choice Scarf Victini fits predominantly on bulky offense and sun teams, where its ability to clean up late-game and pivot into breakers is appreciated. Victini finds itself vulnerable to defensive pieces such as Landorus-T and Ting-Lu, both of which can switch in on V-create and threaten Victini with Earthquake, meaning that Flying-type partners such as Gliscor, Tornadus-T, and Zapdos are appreciated. Dragonite can also switch into Victini comfortably and use it as setup fodder, meaning answers to it such as Clefable are appreciated. As well as this, due to Victini's lack of Heavy-Duty Boots, entry hazards such as Stealth Rocks and Spikes make it hard for Victini to come in and pivot, meaning hazard removal options such as Great Tusk, Defog Landorus-T, and Terapagos are appreciated, with the former two also threatening Heatran for it. In return, Victini can threaten Grass-types such as Ferrothorn and Serperior for them. Victini can often find itself struggling to break through bulky Water-types such as Toxapex and Alomomola, meaning Pokemon that threaten these such as Tapu Koko and Tapu Lele are appreciated, with Victini in return breaking through Steel-types such as Gholdengo, Ferrothorn, and Kingambit for them. Tapu Lele also provides an immunity to Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Urshifu-R's Aqua Jet, while Tapu Koko can pivot into Victini directly with U-turn. Victini also appreciates the sun support of Mega Charizard Y, as it boosts the power of its V-create to new heights, allowing it to OHKO Galarian Slowking and Zapdos after chip damage, with Victini in return being able to use U-turn to pivot into it against foes such as Alomomola and Landorus-T, giving it more opportunities to break.

movesets.name: Pivot
movesets.description:
Victini solidifies itself as an effective pivot, having the ability to defensively check foes like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant as well as force switches with its coverage options. Bolt Strike grants it the opportunity to hit Water-types like Toxapex, Slowbro, and Alomomola that would otherwise try to switch in on its V-create in addition to targeting Moltres and Mega Charizard Y. U-turn lets Victini pivot out against switch-ins such as Mega Latios and Ting-Lu. Encore discourages the use of status moves from slower foes such as Gliscor, Zapdos, and the aforementioned Toxapex. It also prevents Pokemon like Zamazenta from setting up on Victini for free. Toxic is another possible option that allows Victini to put checks like Landorus-T, Mega Latios, and Great Tusk on a timer. One last potential option is Glaciate, hitting Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Dragonite and preventing them from being reliable switch-ins; it also stops Victini from being complete setup fodder for the latter.

Victini finds itself on a plethora of bulky offense and balance teams. These teams appreciate Victini's coverage options putting pressure on common defensive Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Alomomola, and Moltres, which many teams rely on to check offensive threats. Kingambit values Victini as a partner, as they overwhelm shared checks like Alomomola, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T. Additionally, Victini is a good check to Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant, and Kingambit answers foes such as Mega Tyranitar. Victini is vulnerable to faster threats such as Ogerpon-W and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, so checks such as Raging Bolt and Mega Venusaur are appreciated. In return, Victini provides a switch-in against Fairy- and Psychic-type foes like Tapu Lele, which not many Pokemon can reliably switch into. If Victini is not running Glaciate, it is vulnerable to Dragon-types such as Garchomp and Dragonite, as they can use it as setup fodder; therefore, partners like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant are effective, both of which also beat Dark-types like Mega Tyranitar and Kingambit. They're also great speed control options that help assist Victini, as it is outsped by a plethora of foes, the most notable being Ogerpon-W and Mega Diancie. Tapu Koko is another ally that is able to outspeed the Pokemon that threaten Victini like Ogerpon-W and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. It also provides a useful boost to Victini's Bolt Strike in Electric Terrain and forms a strong VoltTurn core with it that overwhelms defensive Pokemon like Galarian Slowking, Ferrothorn, and Heatran. Hisuian Samurott is also an effective partner, as it is able to set Spikes for Victini via Ceaseless Edge, which is beneficial because many of Victini's checks lack Heavy-Duty Boots like Ting-Lu, Garchomp, and Heatran.

movesets.name: Z Celebrate
movesets.description:
Z-Celebrate Victini acts as a niche setup sweeper, where its combination of Z-Celebrate and Stored Power can make it a threatening late-game cleaner. Z-Celebrate's omniboost makes Victini a potent sweeper due to its enhanced bulk and offenses making it difficult to revenge kill. When combined with Z-Celebrate, Stored Power becomes able to muscle through neutral targets such as Landorus-T and Alomomola while also breaking Toxapex, which would otherwise be able to shut down Victini with Haze. Focus Blast is used in order to hit Heatran, Mega Tyranitar, and Ting-Lu, all of which could otherwise comfortably switch in on Victini, with the latter being able to phase it out via Whirlwind, removing its boosts entirely.

Z-Celebrate Victini fits exclusively on hyper offense, where its ability to clean late-game is appreciated. Victini can often find it hard to find setup opportunities against faster foes such as Ogerpon-W and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, so teammates that can pressure these such as Raging Bolt and Booster Energy Iron Valiant are appreciated. In return, Victini can break through Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Melmetal for these. Victini can also often struggle to break through Pokemon that resist its STAB moves, such as Mega Latios and Slowbro, meaning Dark-types such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott are appreciated. In return, Victini can come in on Fighting- and Fairy-types such as Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant and find setup opportunities on them. Victini also appreciates entry hazard support from leads such as Glimmora, Landorus-T, and Mega Diancie in order to whittle down any of its answers, enabling it to clean late-game, while also denying opposing hazards, which is appreciated as Victini finds itself vulnerable to Stealth Rock. Dual screens support from setters like Tapu Koko is also appreciated in order to let it set up on Pokemon that would otherwise threaten it such as Non-Ghostium Z Gholdengo and Mega Diancie.

movesets.name: Pivot
movesets.description: Heavy-Duty Boots Victini is a great offensive pivot, using the combination of its strong V-create, utility options, and momentum to wear down opposing teams. Bolt Strike provides crucial coverage against Water-types such as Slowbro and Volcanion that may try to soak up its other moves. It also OHKOes Mega Aerodactyl, which otherwise takes its other moves quite well and outspeeds it. Toxic is used in the last moveslot to give Victini a way of applying long-term pressure against certain physically defensive pivots such as Hippowdon and Rotom-W that otherwise don't mind taking V-create, allowing Victini to outlast them in the long run. Alternatively, Will-O-Wisp deals less residual damage against the aforementioned targets but it allows Victini to deter physical attackers such as Tyranitar and Azumarill from switching in while creating mind games against Pursuit Tyranitar. Encore is also an interesting option that allows Victini to continue breaking down Pokemon such as Clefable and Mega Latias that rely on stalling V-create via recovery moves while letting Victini double as an effective countermeasure against their setup variants. This Victini set typically fits best on bulkier team structures, which can provide it with sufficient opportunities to break down the opposing team as well as provide a solid defensive foundation for it to fall back on against potential adversaries such as Mega Aerodactyl and Keldeo. Additionally, these structures also appreciate Victini's ability to help play around dangerous threats such as Iron Crown, Clefable, and Mega Gardevoir. Entry hazard setters such as Hippowdon, Clefable, and Skarmory are prime examples that can also support Victini through their use of status moves or, in Clefable's case, Knock Off to remove opposing Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as Rotom-W and Skeledirge. Similarly, other defensive pivots such as Rotom-W, Scizor, Assault Vest Tangrowth, and Celesteela can assist Victini by sponging attacks from the likes of faster Pokemon that may force Victini out, such as Iron Boulder and Shadow Ball Alakazam. Lastly, additional pivoting support, particularly from the aforementioned Rotom-W and Scizor as well as Zeraora and Choice Scarf Mienshao can form effective VoltTurn cores with Victini, utilizing their ability to help force out the likes of Iron Boulder and Mega Aerodactyl in order to compensate for Victini’s lower Speed tier. These Pokemon also appreciate Victini's own ability to lure in and wear down several of the walls that may deter them from making progress, such as Hippowdon, Mega Latias, and Pecharunt.

movesets.name: Choice Band (Psychic)
movesets.description: Victini is a great wallbreaker on Psychic teams due to its well-rounded coverage and signature move in V-create, easing the matchup against Steel, Grass, and Ice teams. Bolt Strike threatens bulky Water-types such as Toxapex, Slowbro, and Tapu Fini that resist V-create. U-turn preserves Psychic's momentum and allows Victini to switch out of Pokemon that wall it like Dragonite and Mega Altaria. Trick cripples common switch-ins such as Storm Drain Gastrodon, Toxapex, and Skeledirge, while Brick Break lets Victini further threaten Steel and Dark teams by hitting Heatran and Mega Tyranitar hard. Choice Scarf Tapu Lele is an excellent teammate due to its ability to check Dark- and Dragon-types like Weavile, Kommo-o, and Hydreigon. It also sets up Psychic Terrain, protecting Victini from priority moves from the likes of Mimikyu and Azumarill. Jirachi and Celebi aid in Victini's wallbreaking by setting up Stealth Rock and replenishing its HP with Healing Wish. Furthermore, they form a pivot core with Victini that deals sizable chip damage while keeping momentum. Latias also provides Healing Wish support and removes entry hazards with Defog to preserve Victini's longevity. Mega Gallade and Victini can each weaken certain physical walls for the other to dispose of such as Ting-Lu and Skeledirge. Deoxys-S breaks through roadblocks like Toxapex, Garchomp, and Swampert and aids in cleaning weakened Flying and Water teams. Slowbro switches into most Water- and Ground-types that threaten Victini, like Urshifu-R and Excadrill, and it brings Victini into the field with Teleport.

movesets.name: Z-Celebrate (Fire)
movesets.description: Victini is an excellent user of Z-Celebrate, which not only boosts its natural bulk, but also its amazing offensive potential. Stored Power in tandem with Z-Celebrate can easily shred through bulky Pokemon such as Toxapex and Gliscor. Focus Blast is a great form of coverage for Victini, as it can break down Dark-, Rock-, and Steel-types such as Tyranitar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Heatran; its low accuracy is also boosted by Victory Star. Alternatively, after a boost, Thunderbolt can threaten Water- and Flying-type Pokemon such as non-Choice Scarf Greninja, Pelipper, and Mega Charizard Y. Torkoal is an excellent teammate to pair with Victini, as not only does it provide sun to boost Victini's Searing Shot, notably giving it a favorable roll to take out Tapu Lele after a boost, but it also provides entry hazard removal in Rapid Spin. Torkoal can also set Stealth Rock of its own, which breaks Sturdy of foes like Skarmory and Ogerpon-C, allowing Victini to sweep. Cinderace can break through bulky Pokemon such as Blissey with itsLibero-boosted STAB High Jump Kick while also using Court Change to remove hazards for Victini. Rotom-H provides an immunity to Ground-types with Levitate and assists by setting up dual screens, letting Victini take advantage of them to set up; it also has a niche in being another hazard removal teammate with Defog. Volcarona's Bug typing and access to Quiver Dance and Bug Buzz can check threatening Dark-types such as Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Hydreigon. Mega Charizard X is a powerful wallbreak that, paired alongside Victini, can take out Dragon-type threats such as Dragonite after its Multiscale is worn down and Kyurem. Ceruledge is another offensive setup sweeper that can take out Ghost-type Pokemon like Blacephalon and a weakened Iron Boulder with Shadow Sneak.

movesets.name: Heavy-Duty Boots (Psychic)
movesets.description: Victini straps on its Heavy-Duty Boots to ignore entry hazards set by Steel, Fairy, and Flying teams, which limit its progress-making capabilities. Bolt Strike synergizes with V-create, targeting Water- and Flying-types like Toxapex and Gyarados. Substitute eases the Steel and Flying matchups by reducing the need for predictions and ensuring that Victini can deal damage to Heatran or Gliscor by scaring out Ferrothorn or Corviknight. Toxic puts walls like Porygon2 and Slowbro on a timer. Encore prevents slower setup users like Swords Dance Iron Hands and Nasty Plot Hydreigon from gaining momentum while also locking defensive foes like Corviknight and Gliscor into unfavorable moves. Power-Up Punch is effective in conjunction with Substitute, as it provides Victini with enough firepower to break through walls in subsequent turns, allowing it to OHKO Gliscor with V-create at +1 after Stealth Rock damage and 2HKO Slowbro and Heatran with Bolt Strike. If these extra wallbreaking capabilities are unnecessary, U-turn lets Victini pivot out of Heatran or Swampert. Victini finds it hard to break through dedicated physical walls like Hippowdon and Archaludon and Dragon-types like Dragonite, so teammates like Latios and Choice Specs Tapu Lele that deal with these are excellent teammates . Setup sweepers like Mega Gallade, Mega Latias, Iron Boulder, and Celebi can find use with Victini locking walls like Ferrothorn and Toxapex into unfavorable moves, and they also remove Landorus, Archaludon, Mega Swampert, and Ogerpon-W. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder provides speed control, hammering fast threats like Mega Lopunny, Choice Scarf Greninja, and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon. Slowbro and Galarian Slowking are decent walls that safely pivot Victini in; Slowbro also takes on scary Ground- and Water-types like Excadrill and Barraskewda, while Galarian Slowking is able to set Toxic Spikes and check Iron Valiant and Keldeo. Jirachi provides hazards and deals with Mega Diancie and Kyurem; in return, Victini deals with Gholdengo and Mega Scizor.
